Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided extracted text, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install-time setup.py/PEP 517 build hook execution, or malicious import-time side effects.
  • The model download and initialization logic appears to be runtime functionality triggered when users call library features, not malicious code that runs during installation or interpreter startup.
  • pyproject.toml appears in the manifest but its contents were not included in the provided corpus, so full verification of build configuration and entry points is limited.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** No evidence was found in the provided files of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets.
  • **Archive staging / exfiltration:** Use of tarfile, .tar.gz, and temporary files is tied to model archive download and cache extraction. download_file_from_gcs() restricts URLs to https://storage.googleapis.com/, blocks redirects, and includes MD5 integrity checking, so this does not plausibly indicate staging or exfiltration of stolen data.
  • **Network exfiltration:** HuggingFace Hub and Google Cloud Storage access are expected model acquisition behavior for this package. No attacker C2, webhook, raw IP, paste/drop-service upload, or suspicious upload endpoint was identified.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile modification, startup-folder registration, or background persistence loops was found.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes service-account use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata probing, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection was found.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** base64.b64decode() is used to decode the GCS x-goog-hash MD5 header. The eval match is llama_cpp.Llama.eval() for model inference, with an inline comment clarifying it is not Python eval(). No exec, dynamic loader, encrypted payload execution, or staged malware loader evidence was found.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • .github/workflows, uv.lock, tests, documentation, and model-management code appear consistent with a normal open-source Python package.
